items.summary: NVIDIA announced two open source projects in public preview, NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR), which together build and operate managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure. NVKE provides software to run a managed service with APIs for provisioning clusters, while NVKR builds reproducible node images from version-pinned sources. Both are Apache 2.0 licensed components of the DSX AI Factory Platform. The projects remain in public preview, may change between releases, and are not yet recommended for production workloads. NVIDIA Cloud Partners Firmus and SK Telecom, plus partners Mirantis, Rafay, Spectro Cloud, OpenNebula Systems, and vCluster, are integrating them into their offerings.
items.title: NVIDIA Announces Open Source Kubernetes Engine for GPU Infrastructure

items.summary: NVIDIA introduced Snapshot, an open-source checkpoint and restore system for GPU workloads on Kubernetes as part of the DSX AI Factory Platform. It captures fully initialized CPU and GPU memory so replicas can resume in seconds instead of minutes during cold starts. Design partners reported large gains: Crusoe cut GLM Pod readiness from roughly 8 minutes to 31 seconds, and Saturn Cloud reduced vLLM startup from 2–8.5 minutes to 6–34 seconds on NVIDIA HGX B300 hardware. Across tested configurations Snapshot restored replicas under 45 seconds—8x to 36x faster than cold start—and checkpoint plus restore was shorter than a single cold start in every case.
items.title: NVIDIA Snapshot Cuts GPU Workload Startup Times

items.summary: Meta introduced Your algorithm, an end-to-end suite of AI-powered tools that makes Facebook recommendations more transparent and steerable through a single editable view. The system lets users state interests in their own words across Feed and Reels via Interested In and Not Interested In lists, with changes applied responsively at every stage from profile generation to LLM reranking and device-level cache invalidation. Meta describes it as creating a more personalized experience informed by both behavior and stated intent, while noting remaining opportunities such as better interpreting ambiguous input and exploring additional entry points for shaping preferences.
items.title: Meta Unveils Your Algorithm for Personalized, Transparent Recommendations

items.summary: At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, NVIDIA is deepening its open source commitment by donating the autonomous-agent security runtime OpenShell to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) as a Sandbox project. It also contributes to Agent Substrate, a Google-led framework for scaling agent workloads on Kubernetes, and announces new DSX AI Factory Platform components: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine and Recipes in public preview, plus NVIDIA Snapshot for faster inference startup. Linux Foundation CEO Jim Zemlin noted the community now faces secure environments for agents. Design partners reported reduced readiness times—Crusoe cut GLM-5.3 from about eight minutes to 31 seconds; Saturn Cloud lowered vLLM startup between two and 8.5 minutes to six and 34 seconds. NVIDIA frames these moves as advancing Kubernetes as the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale.
items.title: NVIDIA Donates OpenShell and Expands Kubernetes AI Offerings at KubeCon

items.summary: Google unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), the TPU 8tx, developed with AMD, and the TPU 8i Max. The company said in a blog post that these chips broaden its portfolio to confidential inference and greater memory capacity for large workloads, aiming to reduce reliance on externally made chips for cloud computing. Google noted the launch arrives as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, OpenAI and Anthropic develop their own semiconductors amid Nvidia’s dominance; reports also cited Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitting an affair with someone alleged to be a Chinese spy.
items.title: Google Unveils Two New AI Chips for Confidential Inference and Larger Workloads

items.summary: Hugging Face now lets organizations link their Hugging Face account to a Google Cloud billing account, so usage appears on the existing Google Cloud invoice instead of requiring a separate credit card. The change is available through the Google Cloud Marketplace and covers Team or Enterprise subscriptions plus pay-as-you-go compute and storage. Until an organization's subscription is approved by the Hugging Face team, any paid usage continues to be billed through its current payment method.
items.title: Hugging Face Adds Google Cloud Billing Option for Organizations

items.summary: Google announced that Gemini 4 Carbon is now available, positioning it as its strongest model with frontier cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across software engineering and scientific reasoning. The company says Carbon ranks #1 on CursorBench 4. 0, Perplexity’s WANDR and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model, though it pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It is available via API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens — the same introductory price as Argon — and is rolling out to Ultra subscribers across Antigravity, the app and Search. In simulated cyberattack testing environments seeded with ExploitBench and CyScenarioBench, Carbon blocked 99% of attack trajectories from Google’s adaptive red-teaming agent (down from 3. 1% on Argon), lowering the per-attempt breach rate to just 0. 8%.
items.title: Google Makes Gemini 4 Carbon Available

items.summary: Anthropic is pursuing a stock market flotation valuing the company at up to $1.4tn (£1.05tn), below the $2tn previously expected, after investors questioned AI-boom durability following midterm election wins for datacentre opponents. A US regulatory filing on Tuesday reported the lower target; trading could begin next week. The company plans to raise up to $64.4bn by selling 825m shares at up to $78 each, with a further $26bn via private placement involving Alphabet and Nvidia.
items.title: Anthropic Sets $1.4tn Valuation Ahead of IPO

items.summary: At Web Summit in Lisbon, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted on stage that he had an affair with a Chinese datacenter executive suspected to be a Beijing spy. The disclosure sent Nvidia shares down 7.5% at the open, wiping over $330bn off its value. Cloudflare's Matthew Prince framed the episode as a threat to Nvidia's market dominance and questioned whether its financing practices were legitimate financial engineering. Huang apologized in an employee letter; his board launched an independent investigation into national security concerns. The article also examines Silicon Valley tech leaders attempting reconciliation with newly elected Democrats after last month's elections.
items.title: Nvidia CEO affair and tech's political reckoning

items.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2.5, a robotic AI platform it says is approaching human-level performance on real-world tasks. The version scored a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate and was 20 to 30 percent faster than the prior release in laboratory tests across more than 200 activities. Powered by Gemini Robotics 2.5, Apptronik’s Apollo 2 robots tied bows and reached a 96 percent success rate kitting parts at Mercedes-Benz factories in Europe. DeepMind director Kanishka Rao called closing the remaining gap to human performance “a steep road.”
items.title: DeepMind Unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5 With Safety Benchmark

items.summary: Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which adds the assistant to video calls so it can draft plans while participants talk. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets for real-time collaboration. These launches follow similar tools from OpenAI and Meta as AI vendors compete with Microsoft and Google over office suites.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Meetings and Other Workplace Tools in Beta

items.summary: Apple released twelve software updates on Tuesday, patching wireless security flaws in Bluetooth pairing, AirPlay connection rate limits, and Messages across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and VisionOS. Apple’s notes say the fixes address issues like unauthorized group-chat joins and PIN brute-forcing; some vulnerabilities were found internally while others came from researchers. Reports link two of them to earlier studies by French researchers and Oligo.
items.title: Apple Ships Twelve Security Patches for Wireless Flaws Across Its Devices

items.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind used an AI system called AlphaProof Code, built on the Gemini Carbon model, to formally verify portions of Signal’s underlying cryptographic code. The work mathematically proved that parts of the encrypted messaging app’s code function as intended without errors — a task completed in about a month that might normally take experts years. It builds on earlier verification by the Signal Foundation and is open-sourced; DeepMind did not release it as a consumer product, though WhatsApp and Google Messages use similar encryption.
items.title: Google DeepMind uses AI to verify Signal encryption

items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer introduced Mitra-v2, the second generation of a tabular foundation model pretrained on synthetic tables. Unlike earlier tools that require per-table setup, one pretrained model reads labeled rows from an unseen table and predicts the rest via in-context learning. The architecture is unchanged; pretraining now uses tables with 10 times as many rows and roughly three times as many columns as Mitra-v1, plus a new hybrid synthetic prior. On TabArena, a public benchmark of 51 real-world datasets maintained by an independent academic team, Mitra-v2 leads the single-model field, outperforming Mitra-v1 on 32 of 33 shared datasets and completing all 51 within one hour. It also ranks first among fine-tuned models on ScoringBench for regression.
items.title: Amazon Connect Customer launches Mitra-v2 tabular foundation model

items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, the same underlying model offered at two safeguard levels. Fable adds classifiers that block high-risk cybersecurity tasks and most research biology so it can reach all users; Mythos drops those blocks but requires membership in Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program and Life Sciences Verification Program. When Fable blocks a query, users receive an answer from Opus 4.8 (cyber) or Opus 5 (biology). All benchmark scores are self-reported by Anthropic and not independently verified; for example, Fable scored 64.9% on RoboDojo Sim versus GPT-6 Astra's 29.8%, while AutomationBench showed Gemini 4 Carbon ahead at 53.9% to Fable's 51.4%. Pricing starts at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with a fast mode priced higher.
items.title: Anthropic Ships Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 With Different Safeguards

items.summary: The Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Nov 10 that the Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October after advancing 0.6% in September, below economists polled by Reuters who had expected a 0.3% gain. Core CPI climbed 0.3%, matching forecasts. The article notes inflation remains above the Fed's 2% target and left markets pricing a December rate increase.
items.title: US October CPI rises above forecast, Fed set for December rate hike

items.summary: The Ministry of Transport responded to a letter questioning new financing restrictions on individually owned private-hire cars that took effect Oct 30, 2026. The rules treat such vehicles like other privately owned cars because they serve both personal and hire purposes. Changes aim for consistent treatment while preventing over-leveraging. The ministry will monitor arrangements including in-house loans and long-term leasing against the 100% business loans.
items.title: MOT Clarifies Financing Rules for Individually Owned Private-Hire Cars

items.summary: The Singapore Food Agency, via Senior Director Cheong Lai Peng, responds to Liu Fook Thim's letter calling for affordable local vegetables at shopping venues. The agency notes that while local farms support food resilience and supply buffers, they face higher land and manpower costs than imported alternatives. SFA is working with the Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation on productivity gains, technology adoption, aggregation, and new sales channels to improve price competitiveness.
items.title: SFA Commits to Affordable Local Produce

items.summary: GitHub rewrote the software engine behind several Copilot products, porting its codebase from TypeScript to Rust using GitHub Copilot itself. The effort was triggered by heavy resource use and difficulty embedding Copilot elsewhere; a full rewrite would have needed many developers over about two years. Using the Copilot app, CLI, and AI agents, one developer finished it in a few months. An early estimate put porting at roughly 130K lines, but more logic moved out of the interface layer, so ultimately around 430K lines were migrated. The rewrite cut client lifecycle time from about 5.25 seconds to 292 milliseconds and raised throughput from 7.55 to 120 completed session lifecycles per second; in a 10-client test peak private memory fell from roughly 1383 MB to 126 MB.
items.title: GitHub Rewrote Copilot’s Engine in Months With AI

items.summary: TypeSafe AI introduced Jev, a decision model that returns structured decisions and probabilities instead of generating text token by token. Hugging Face now supports the interface through transformers classes and llama.cpp, aiming to agree on a common contract without forcing one implementation.
items.title: Hugging Face Introduces Decision Models for LLMs

items.summary: CPCA data shows Tesla wholesaled only 8,817 cars in China from Giga Shanghai in October, the lowest domestic level since July 2022. Of 67,829 vehicles built that month, 59,012 were exports, leaving just 8,817 for Chinese buyers—down 66% year-over-year and 86% from September's 64,837. Analysts note Tesla front-loads export orders early in each quarter while pushing domestic deliveries later; October is the first month of a new quarter. Still, Electrek argues the cycle alone cannot explain why this October was less than half any other this year or one-third of last October's 26,006 low. Through October, China sales fell 15% to 389,905 cars while Giga Shanghai exports rose 101% to 420,984—more abroad than at home for the first time. Beijing plans to cut EV export VAT rebates from 13% to 9% on April 1, 2027, which may pressure automakers to front-load shipments further.
items.title: Tesla China Domestic Sales Collapse as Exports Surge

items.summary: Carbon Brief analysis of provisional UNFCCC lists shows more than 92,000 people registered for COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, potentially the largest COP ever. Party delegates number 18,812; including overflow raises that to over 34,000. Host nation Turkey sent 2,950 people, ahead of Brazil (1,994), Nigeria and China. The UNFCCC will release final figures after the summit.
items.title: COP31 registration tops previous summits as host nation leads delegate counts

items.summary: The Senate voted Monday, the article states, to advance bipartisan permitting legislation known as BAAJA of 2026. The vote tally was reported as 73-25. Supporters say it speeds approval for high-voltage transmission lines that currently take an average of 10 years to build and could create over 100,000 trades jobs. Opponents warn the bill weakens legal tools used against fossil fuel projects and may raise emissions. Democrats who voted said they want further changes before final passage; Sen. Jeff Merkley opposed moving forward. The measure still must pass the House and awaits a favorable Trump administration stance on wind energy.
items.title: Senate Clears Energy Permitting Bill Amid Fossil-Fuel and Clean-Energy Tension

items.summary: On Nov. 10, Anthropic announced it was bringing its Claude assistant into video conferencing platform Google Meet as part of a wider effort to embed AI in office work. The feature, called Claude Meetings, lets users add Claude to calls so it can follow discussions and turn them into tasks, timelines and answers live. It launches in beta for Team and Enterprise customers through Google Meet before expanding elsewhere.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Claude Assistant to Google Meet for Live Meeting Tasks

items.summary: On Tuesday, IBM announced it was ending US visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of roles in IBM Consulting, which employs more than 150,000 people. The decision follows heightened scrutiny of foreign tech hiring under Donald Trump's administration, which last month suspended several companies from the Permanent Labor Certification process. A company spokesperson said participation in high-skilled visa programs has declined over years as skill availability and client needs have evolved.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa and Green Card Sponsorship for Most Consulting Roles

items.summary: Kunal Shah, WhatsApp's global head since June 2026, outlined three priorities on Tuesday: more expressive conversations, simpler financial and everyday transactions, and AI to help users complete tasks. He said his first four months focused on understanding what the platform's over three billion users want.
items.title: WhatsApp chief Kunal Shah reveals platform priorities

items.summary: Columnist Liz asks how a CEO who delivered 700,000% returns could be removed, noting President Donald Trump believes Jensen Huang should keep his job. Prediction markets currently price about 14% odds of firing by year's end, though the author hedges that Nvidia shares may recover within weeks. The board runs its own investigation into who knew what and when.
items.title: Trump backs Jensen Huang amid Nvidia spy scandal

items.summary: On Diwali night Delhi's PM2.5 hit 3,744 micrograms per cubic metre in Mundka, with 125 CPCB readings missing and official AQI questioned; NASA satellite captured haze over northern India while a Yamuna river safari began.
items.title: Delhi pollution tops 3,744 as Nvidia chief faces spy probe

items.summary: The New York Fed's Center for Microeconomic Data reports that credit card delinquency rose sharply between 2022 and 2024, with the steepest increases among borrowers in lower-income neighborhoods. The analysis accompanies the latest Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit, which shows total nominal household debt balances increased by $334 billion in Q3 2026, a 1.8 percent rise from Q2 2026. During the pandemic, new cards went increasingly to lower-income borrowers with weaker credit scores; those accounts now show higher distress as forbearances and stimulus faded.
items.title: New York Fed Finds Credit Card Delinquency Widening by Income After 2022

items.summary: President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating Nvidia's chief executive over an alleged affair with a person tied to Chinese intelligence, widening fallout from the scandal around the world's largest chipmaker. Shares fell after Jensen Huang admitted infidelity with an executive linked to Chinese intelligence. Lawmakers in a soon-to-be Democrat-controlled Congress have pledged investigations, and the Commerce Department has reportedly begun preparing new semiconductor export controls.
items.title: Trump Says FBI Investigating Nvidia CEO Over Alleged Chinese Spy Link

items.summary: Anthropic released its Economic Index report, which identifies six patterns in how people use the AI tool Claude, from tax-day rushes to weekend chats. The findings show that personal conversations make up about 35% on weekdays and nearly 50% on weekends; at 6 p.m., recipe requests occur at 2.3 times the average rate; and before the April 14 filing deadline, tax questions reached eight times their usual May share. Work output differs by context: documents appear in 20% of work conversations versus explanations at 17%. Higher-paid workers consume 2.07 times more tokens than lower-paid ones. Michael S. Barr notes little evidence that AI displaces jobs. Anthropic's researchers suggest automation may be labor-augmenting, while Federal Reserve Board economists Leland D. Crane and Paul E. Soto find coder employment growth about 3 percent lower since ChatGPT arrived. Managers over-represent the survey respondents at 23% versus 7% of U.S. employment, which could skew optimism among heavy users.
items.title: Anthropic's Economic Index Reveals Six Patterns in Claude Use

items.summary: Journalist Mona Chalabi, in her book Ten Lives, describes financial insecurity felt across the U.S. economic spectrum after profiling 10 Americans over five years. She says nearly everyone she interviewed expressed a sense of panic about their finances, which she links to what she calls an especially precarious American system. Chalabi also notes that many profiled people identified as middle class regardless of actual income and considered parental wealth central to their own economic security. The piece is drawn from interview highlights covering partner selection trends and her transparency about compensation.
items.title: Author Frames Widespread Financial Anxiety as American 'Panic',

items.summary: On Tuesday, Kemi Badenoch and Helen Whately held a press conference in Westminster explaining plans to cut £36.1bn from the welfare budget, with up to £10,000 per household removed. The article frames the announcement as an opposition party re-announcing figures previously discussed at the Conservative party conference last month, noting such costings are rarely taken seriously and may fail before Christmas. Whately presented the numbers while dismissing charities’ warnings of a surge in child poverty and acknowledging only limited compassion for terminally ill or retired claimants. The piece satirises the government’s approach without independent verification of its economic claims.
items.title: Badenoch and Whately Outline Welfare Budget Cuts

items.summary: Retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator reports that sales of bottled water, hand sanitiser and tinned goods rose in the ten days following the government's 'Be Ready' emergency preparedness campaign launch on 22 October. Fraser McKevitt says shoppers took notice but were not panic buying. The firm disputes claims of stockpiling frenzy, attributing growth to households adding recommended items to their weekly shop.
items.title: UK sales of tinned food and water rise after emergency preparedness campaign launch

items.summary: Jensen Huang, chief executive and co-founder of Nvidia, admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, who has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. Nvidia is the world's largest supplier of high-end AI chips, with some estimates placing its market share over 80%. Sales of its most powerful chips to China have been restricted since 2022, though relaxed last year. Trade records indicate over US$3 billion in chips crossed from Singapore to China in a single year. Nvidia's share price fell after the disclosure, and it is reportedly under criminal investigation while Congress requests Huang explain his interactions with Alice Huang.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal and AI Chip Fallout

items.summary: In an episode of Leaders Talk, CMG's Zou Yun spoke with Alexander De Croo, administrator of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), about China's development achievements and its role in advancing global sustainable development. They explored how the CIIE can create new opportunities for international cooperation and examined how China's commitment to high-standard opening-up may benefit the world.
items.title: UNDP Administrator Discusses China's Role in Global Development

items.summary: A CGTN opinion piece by Liu Chunsheng argues that China's October consumer price index rise of 0.7% year-on-year and core CPI gain of 0.8%, both easing, reflect a K-shaped split rather than broad demand recovery. He notes the headline is driven mainly by energy and AI-related electronics, while food prices keep falling and industrial goods stay flat. The producer price index rose 5.7% in October as profits of large industrial firms grew 15.5% over nine months against retail sales rising just 1.1%. Core CPI staying below 1% shows demand-driven recovery has not yet appeared, so the author calls for raising household incomes and expanding domestic demand rather than relying on rate cuts alone.
items.title: China's CPI recovery masks price divergence, commentator says

items.summary: Sources briefed on UK government proposals say a substantial expansion of the under-16s social media ban, set to come into force in March, could inadvertently extend coverage to platforms such as YouTube Kids, Lego Play, Spotify and games services. One source close to the talks said up to 150 platforms may now be covered. The regulations are expected for cabinet signoff this week, with culture secretary Lisa Nandy due to lay them in parliament in December. Tech companies argue that removing recommender systems would make their sites non-functional, prompting calls for clearer guidelines.
items.title: UK social media ban expansion could cover YouTube Kids and other sites

items.summary: Israel's newly sworn-in parliament has begun competing over who will form the next government, with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot tasked by President Isaac Herzog after receiving more Knesset recommendations than outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Both blocs fell short of a majority in the 120-seat body: Eisenkot's four parties won 48 seats and Netanyahu's won 53. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible two-week extension, to build a coalition. Arab-led alliances gained an unprecedented 19 seats between them, potentially holding the balance of power, while ultra-Orthodox parties oppose conscription reforms central to Eisenkot's four principles. Netanyahu and Eisenkot exchanged sharp warnings about governing across ideological lines as uncertainty over the outcome grows.
items.title: Eisenkot Tasked With Forming Government After New Knesset Swearing-In

items.summary: A reporter travels with a Ukrainian drone unit called Peaky Blinders into the heavily bombed city of Slovyansk, in eastern Ukraine's Donetsk region. The team escorts them through constant bombardment from Russian drones and glide bombs, past rubble and abandoned vehicles destroyed by remotely operated drones. Slovyansk is one of four cities forming Ukraine's 'fortress belt', central to resumed peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US after nine months, which Ukrainian officials say Kyiv refuses to cede territory over. The unit's commander Oleksandr rejects Russia's claim that seizing the Donbas will end the war, while resident Alina Shyrko coordinates civilian evacuations as families leave amid deteriorating conditions.
items.title: Ukraine's drone unit holds devastated Slovyansk amid evacuation

items.summary: On the 88th anniversary of Kristallnacht, also known as the Night of Broken Glass, a pogrom against Jewish populations in Nazi Germany and Austria that escalated toward the Holocaust, Friedrich Merz stated that Germany now confronts a historic test over antisemitism.
items.title: Merz marks Kristallnacht anniversary as Germany faces antisemitism test

items.summary: French students vow to maintain protest pressure for improved learning conditions, following months of demonstrations that began in September over school renovations and university reforms before broadening into cost-of-living protests involving trade unions and political activists.
items.title: French Students Promise Continued Protests Over School Conditions

items.summary: Climate activist Greta Thunberg arrived Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, at the U.N. climate summit (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey. She urged protecting people and the planet over profits and power, calling current systems “incompatible with human nature.” This is her first U.N. climate summit since the 2021 COP in Glasgow, Scotland; she had previously attended a 2024 protest rally against Azerbaijan hosting that year’s talks.
items.title: Greta Thunberg Arrives at COP31 Climate Talks in Antalya

items.summary: At this year's UN climate talks in Antalya, Türkiye promoted its '35 by 35' pledge to raise electricity's share of global energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035. The plan faces resistance because the proposed wording does not require clean or renewable energy to meet the goal. Australia instead advanced a voluntary pledge to double rooftop solar households to at least 300 million by 2030, joined by Bangladesh, Kenya, Nigeria, Palau and Vanuatu. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged leaders to leave clear next steps on a fossil fuel transition roadmap.
items.title: Türkiye's Electrification Pledge Faces Pushback at COP31

items.summary: Iran denied on Tuesday that its Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps carried out a cyberattack on roughly 700 of France's supermarkets, which began overnight October 11-12 and raised refrigerator temperatures. Iran's Foreign Ministry called the accusations baseless while condemning what it termed France projecting governance failures. Paris summoned Tehran's ambassador and said it would seek European-level sanctions; EU spokesman Anouar El Anouni pledged a swift response. French prosecutor Laure Beccuau opened an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC cyber unit.
items.title: Iran Rejects France's Cyberattack Accusations as Paris Escalates Response

items.summary: A new exhibition, 'Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence,' at the German Historical Museum in Berlin explores contested parallels between colonial rule and Nazism. Curator Stephan Malinowski says it aims to tell the story rather than settle an ongoing debate about whether such comparisons risk minimizing Nazi crimes or neglecting Germany's colonial past. It opens amid renewed discussion, including Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice over support for Israel during the war in Gaza. The exhibition runs until April 11, 2027.
items.title: Berlin Exhibition Links Colonial and Nazi Violence Without Equating Them

items.summary: An alleged espionage scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has intensified scrutiny of the company amid the ongoing technology war between Washington and Beijing. The controversy centers on Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, under investigation for suspected diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. While US intelligence assessments raise unproven concerns about her links to Chinese intelligence, Nvidia's board launched an independent probe and denies any compromise of its secrets or national security. Data from research firm IDC shows Nvidia held 34% of China's data-centre AI chip market in the first half of 2026, shipping about 678,000 accelerators versus Huawei's 572,000 (28%). Reports place Megaspeed's purchases at about $4.8 billion over two years. The dispute reflects broader tensions: US export restrictions since October 2022 aim to limit China's access to advanced computing power, while Congress pushes for stronger oversight through proposals like the AI Overwatch Act and Chip Security Act.
items.title: Nvidia Caught Between US Export Rules and China's AI Demand Amid Espionage Probe

items.summary: President Trump defended Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, saying he believes Huang's explanation that he was unaware of former executive Alice Huang's alleged intelligence connections and expected the FBI probe not to damage his position. The defence follows allegations that roughly 240,000 advanced processors were moved into China through intermediaries in a network worth $7.5 billion, which Reuters said it had not independently verified. Nvidia launched an independent board investigation while shareholders filed a proposed class-action lawsuit; shares fell 4.27% to $178.67 Monday and later opened 2.09% higher at $182.40 Tuesday. Lawmakers from both parties pressed for answers, and China dismissed the reports as groundless speculation.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia Chief Amid China Allegations

items.summary: The Supreme Court, in a suo motu case titled ‘In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’, directed WhatsApp and other intermediaries to submit proposed measures against digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant listed the plea for further consideration on November 23. The court emphasised that financial institutions must compensate victims where fraud results from a bank's failure to exercise due diligence, noting cyber crimes fell 50 per cent this year yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far. Banks were described as a protective umbrella with transaction data they should use to prevent fraud before money leaves an account. The bench also directed the RBI and state law enforcement agencies to submit reports and suggestions for prevention and prosecution, and listed the plea for further hearing on November 23.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Intermediaries and Banks on Digital Arrest Scam Prevention

items.summary: The USDA Foreign Agricultural Service office in New Delhi forecasts Indian apple imports to rise about 19 per cent to 5.11 lakh tonnes during the 2026-27 marketing year, driven by rising domestic consumption and stronger demand for high-quality fruit. Consumption is seen growing roughly 5 per cent from a revised 2.76 million tonnes in 2025-26. The outlook follows cautious procurement amid supply volatility; production is expected to grow about 3 per cent at 2.59 million tonnes, supported by favourable conditions in Jammu and Kashmir after weaker yields elsewhere.
items.title: USDA Forecasts Sharp Rise in India's Apple Imports for 2026-27

items.summary: A 60-year-old Danish man, Klaus Elmfelt Aerenlund, filed a lawsuit in San Francisco County Superior Court against OpenAI after following legal advice from ChatGPT. He claims the chatbot told him he could stop paying rent during his dog dispute with his landlord and that losing his home was legally impossible. After three months without payment, he was evicted in June 2026 and lived in his car before finding temporary shelter at a campsite.
items.title: Danish Man Sues OpenAI After ChatGPT Rent Advice Led To Eviction

items.summary: At Lisbon's Web Summit, allegations of Chinese spying on Nvidia overshadowed proceedings. Nvidia shares fell more than five percent in Tuesday afternoon Wall Street trading. Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects spies for China, though Beijing denied the claim. Executives see opportunities amid turmoil; Larry Li noted short-term stock turbulence but possible benefits for rivals like Qualcomm and AMD.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Dominates Web Summit as Shares Fall and Rivals Eye Gains

items.summary: A controversy involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has drawn scrutiny from US authorities, an FBI investigation and a shareholder lawsuit. Reports allege that connections linked to Alice Huang helped route roughly $7.5 billion in AI-chip shipments to Chinese customers, potentially implicating export controls. The New York Times reported the intelligence allegations; Reuters reviewed shipping records showing Megaspeed International's Indonesian subsidiary imported Nvidia processors between 2024 and 2026. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation on November 8 and stated it had no reason to believe trade secrets or national security interests were compromised, while China rejected the espionage claims as unsubstantiated. Nvidia shares fell 4.3% to $178.67 on November 9, reducing its market capitalisation by about $190 billion. The article notes that none of these allegations establish wrongdoing and that questions remain under investigation.
items.title: Nvidia and Jensen Huang face probe over alleged China intelligence links

items.summary: Jensen Huang admitted an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which the author says threatens to inject uncertainty into the AI ecosystem. The piece argues that CEO scandals signal deeper governance risks and succession problems. Nvidia has no clear heir apparent for Huang, who wants decades in his role, and Bloomberg News reported he built an informal structure around himself. The board's early statement on its investigation sounds premature; because Nvidia is a multi-trillion-dollar company centered on one person, any threat to Huang risks the whole enterprise.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Affair Raises Succession Fears

items.summary: An analysis of the Nvidia affair examines how Jensen Huang's reported relationship with Alice Huang, suspected by US intelligence of ties to China, raises concerns about protecting strategically important technology firms from foreign interference. While China denies espionage allegations, Nvidia launched an independent investigation stating no reason to believe sensitive information was compromised.
items.title: Nvidia Affair Raises Questions on AI Security and Succession Planning

items.summary: On the Monday after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, Nvidia stock fell as much as 8 per cent before recovering to about 4 per cent below Friday's close. The probe examined allegations that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation involving a woman suspected of working for China. For three years Nvidia had been the engine of US stocks' rise; analysts now warn the bigger risk may be tighter chip restrictions on China ahead of its November 17 results.
items.title: Nvidia Stock Slides on CEO Probe While Wall Street Rallies

items.summary: Three contract workers died on 9 November 2026 while cleaning a wastewater treatment tank during maintenance at a Tata Electronics factory near Hosur, Tamil Nadu. They collapsed after reportedly inhaling toxic fumes and were declared dead on arrival at a hospital in Hosur. The facility supplies casings for Apple iPhones. B. Akmal (28), M. Sarathi Kumar (28) from Dharmapuri, and Kaveri (30) of Hosur were among the victims. Minister S Keerthana said the incident would be thoroughly investigated.
items.title: Three Workers Die Cleaning Tank at Tata Electronics iPhone Parts Factory

items.summary: The Central Pollution Control Board defended its air quality monitoring methodology, explaining why official AQI readings are capped at 500 despite private apps reporting levels as high as 1,800 in Delhi after Diwali. The board said the ceiling is an intentional feature of the National Air Quality Index (NAQI), consistent with international practices including US EPA scale, since all such levels fall under the 'Severe' category and do not change health advisories.
items.title: CPCB Defends Capping Official Air Quality Index at 500

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat defended traditional Diwali practices, stating earlier firecrackers were free of harmful chemicals and helped eliminate insects while purifying the air. His comments arrive as air quality worsens across Delhi and other metropolitan cities, where fireworks remain a contentious issue over their environmental and health impacts.
items.title: RSS Chief Defends Traditional Diwali Firecrackers Amid Delhi Pollution Crisis
